{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CapyMOA Test and Package

on:
  push:
    branches: [ master, capymoa, main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ master, capymoa, main ]

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up JDK 21
      uses: actions/setup-java@v4
      with:
        java-version: '21'
        distribution: 'microsoft'
        cache: maven

    - name: Unit Tests
      working-directory: ./moa
      run: mvn -B test

    - name: Package Jar
      working-directory: ./moa
      # -B: non-interactive (batch) mode
      # -DskipTests: skip tests (they were run earlier)
      # -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true: skip javadoc generation
      # -Dlatex.skipBuild=true: skip latex documentation build this needs extra dependencies
      run: mvn -B package -DskipTests -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true -Dlatex.skipBuild=true

    # Upload jar file as artifact
    - name: Upload Jar
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: moa-jar
        path: ./moa/target/moa-*-jar-with-dependencies.jar
        if-no-files-found: error
        retention-days: 7",
  "rationale": "The workflow already caches Maven dependencies via actions/setup-java@v4 with cache: maven, so adding a separate actions/cache (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) would be redundant and is contraindicated because an equivalent cache already exists. There is no matrix, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST does not apply. CI history provides representative successful-duration history (5 successful runs, roughly 5.5-7 minutes each), satisfying the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT precondition. Adding timeout-minutes: 30 bounds runaway job consumption with about 4x operational headroom over observed durations while preserving every test, package, and artifact step and all required coverage. It adds no permissions, secrets, deployment/publishing, or new network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
